card.name: Flamenco
card.tagline: Andalusia — Romani fire shaped by Moorish grace. Stamp, clap, cry, until the floor answers.
card.profile: Flamenco (Spanish pronunciation: [flaˈmeŋko]) is an art form based on the various folkloric music traditions of southern Spain, developed within the gitano subculture of the region of Andalusia, and also having historical presence in Extremadura and Murcia. In a wider sense, the term is used to refer to a variety of both contemporary and traditional musical styles typical of southern Spain. Flamenco is closely associated with the gitanos of the Romani ethnicity, who have contributed significantly to its origin and professionalization.
card.insight: in continuous evolution together with rhythm, the poetic stanzas, and the ambiance." On 16 November 2010, UNESCO declared flamenco one of the Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity. The oldest record of flamenco music dates to 1774 in the book Las Cartas Marruecas by José Cadalso.

lessons.title: Complete Intro to Flamenco Dance Class

parts.note: Teacher introduces herself and welcomes beginners to the workshop.
Teacher explains what flamenco is, its origins with the Romani people, and its cultural evolution.
Teacher explains flamenco rhythms (palos) and specifically tangos.
Teacher breaks down the four-count compas and hand clapping (palmas).
Teacher practices palmas along with guitar music.
Teacher explains arm and upper body posture and wrist movement.

steps.name: Hand clapping rhythm in compas
steps.description: Hand clapping in a four-count compas rhythm for tangos.

common_mistakes: Keeping arms straight instead of rounded
Moving arms along with the hands
lessons.teacher_style: The instructor provides detailed cultural background and structure before guiding students step by step. She breaks down complex movements into counts and rhythms using clear demonstrations and verbal counting.
lessons.distinctive_method: Explaining the cultural and musical definition of compas and palos extensively before applying them to physical practice.
what_works: Clear verbal explanations of rhythm and structure
Step-by-step breakdown of counts before adding music
what_hinders: Long periods of talking before physical demonstration

evidence.observation: Teacher stands facing the camera in a dance studio speaking to the audience.
Teacher demonstrates counting with hand gestures.
